races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario but 17 days off turf racing and inconsistent recent form are concerns.

runners_data.name: Merapi
runners_data.note: Closer who showed improved form when runner-up here last time and the extra furlong should suit her well.
runners_data.comment: Half-length second here (1m) last time was her closest finish, running on well from rear
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 last year for Ed Walker; new yard this year and her half-length second of 14 here (good) last time was her closest finish, over 1m but she ran on well from rear; 1m1f, at the least, will be within range on that evidence.

runners_data.name: Shielas Well
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer ideally suited to this trip between 7f-1m3f extremes with Ian Williams' recent guidance.
runners_data.comment: Third run for yard; very well handicapped on plenty of form and has first-time headgear
runners_data.spotlight: With Ian Williams for last two outings, finding 7f too sharp on first occasion and maybe 1m3f too far on second; now she splits the difference and is very well handicapped judged on plenty of form, including a 1m2f win last June; could be dangerous in first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Prince Hector
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to lead throughout but turf form patchy and 51 days since last outing.
runners_data.comment: All three wins on AW, latest last March; rarely seen on turf these days; first tongue-tie
runners_data.spotlight: Not the most consistent and all three career wins were on AW, the latest last March; finished second or third in seven of his last 13 starts but rarely seen on turf these days; tongue tied first time.

runners_data.name: Twilight Guest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 109-day break which raises fitness questions despite solid recent placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Dash Power
runners_data.note: Prominent style should see him well-placed but new connections since last run add an element of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Does not look the percentage call unless the change of trainers sparks something
runners_data.spotlight: Gained sole win (44 races) in a classified in January 2025; eight seconds too, including two on AW this year; changed hands and left Lawrence Mullaney since latest start and that change of scenery needs to spark something.

runners_data.name: Duke Orsino
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden trying longer trip for first time with Oliver Carmichael's 7lb claim potentially significant.
runners_data.comment: 0-11, never always finishing towards rear; cheekpieces latest; now it's a step up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden, never always finishing towards rear; tried cheekpieces on latest start; now it's a step up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Prince Hector will take the field along as the sole confirmed front runner, with Dash Power likely settling prominently just behind. With only seven runners and limited early pace pressure, Prince Hector can dictate a comfortable tempo through the first mile before the race develops. The moderate gallop will suit hold-up horses like Shielas Well, Merapi, and Hibernate who can close strongly in the straight. This race shape strongly favours closers who can benefit from the steady pace and deliver their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Hector sets an uncontested lead allowing closers to wind up.
scenarios.body: The moderate pace plays perfectly into the hands of the hold-up brigade who can unleash sustained finishes. Shielas Well and Merapi benefit most from the tactical setup and trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Prince Hector maintains his lead and the closers leave it too late.
scenarios.body: The eight-year-old's stamina tells as he keeps finding despite the challengers, with Dash Power picking up the pieces. Limited early pace allows the leaders to have enough left in reserve.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Dash Power and other prominent runners time their moves perfectly from mid-pack.
scenarios.body: Those tracking the pace can kick clear before the hold-up horses get into gear. The moderate tempo suits horses who can sit handy and deliver a telling blow two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Orsino or another outsider benefits from the strong pace and trip.
scenarios.body: The slower tempo and step up in distance transforms one of the maidens into a different proposition. Fresh legs and the tactical advantage of being overlooked could pay dividends.

watchPoints.text: Prince Hector's jumping and early pace - if he goes too fast early it transforms the entire race dynamic
Twilight Guest's fitness after 109 days off and whether David Egan can get him competitive from the start
Merapi's ability to reproduce her Yarmouth second under pressure when the pace quickens
Duke Orsino's response to the step up in trip and whether the longer distance brings improvement
Shielas Well's settling pattern early as she needs to be positioned to deliver her customary late charge

races.name: Branfords Restaurant & Bar Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Fashion People
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven 7f form who must overcome 175 days off but has Buick's tactical expertise
runners_data.comment: 1-2 at Newcastle (7f, AW; six ran) in November and she led over 1f out for a clearcut win
runners_data.spotlight: Mehmas first foal of a 7f 2yo winner (RPR 88); 1-2 for her first appearance in a six-runner maiden at Newcastle (7f, AW) in November and she led over 1f out for a clearcut win; promising.

runners_data.name: Baandee
runners_data.note: Natural front runner making turf debut but has consistent all-weather form and faces no pace pressure
runners_data.comment: 2nd in her three starts, all 7f at Chelmsford (AW); from the front on first two occasions
runners_data.spotlight: Second in her three starts, all over 7f at Chelmsford (AW) and from the front on first two occasions; should play a major role if okay on turf.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sky
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up type who showed promise at Newmarket despite poor finishing position
runners_data.comment: Tenth of 11 when 33-1 at Newmarket (7f, good to soft) in November but she showed promise
runners_data.spotlight: 300,000euros yearling by St Mark's Basilica; tenth of 11 when 33-1 for a novice at Newmarket (7f, good to soft) in November but she showed promise to be in touch for 4f and could be the type to do a lot better.

runners_data.name: Night Shining
runners_data.note: Well-bred hold-up horse returning from 294-day break with similar going experience
runners_data.comment: 475,000gns buy; 9-2, sixth of 8 at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) last July but some promise
runners_data.spotlight: 475,000gns yearling by Dark Angel; 9-2, slowly away and never dangerous when about 8l sixth of eight in maiden at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) last July; that's all that was seen of her as a 2yo but she did show some promise.

runners_data.name: Too Too Divine
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with limited ability who faded badly in her sole start
runners_data.comment: Last of four in one AW race; could be a big improver this season, which she needs to be
runners_data.spotlight: 75,000gns yearling by Starman; weak 12-1 for maiden at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in November, chasing the all-the-way winner over 4f before fading into last of four (all from major stables); could be a big improver this season, which she needs to be; market may guide.

runners_data.name: Me An' All
runners_data.note: Weak hold-up horse who was well beaten on recent reappearance and lacks early pace
runners_data.comment: 150-1, beaten 18l in a newcomers race at Newmarket (1m, good) two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: 150-1, beaten 18l in a newcomers race at Newmarket (1m, good) two weeks ago; should improve but hard to fancy just yet.

races.paceDynamic: Baandee will lead from the gate, having made the running in her last two starts at Chelmsford, with no other natural pace setters in this field. Fashion People and the other hold-up horses (Night Shining, Too Too Divine, Me An' All) will settle behind, creating a strung-out formation rather than any early pressure. With only one front runner and a small field, the pace will be measured and controlled, allowing Baandee to dictate terms without harassment. This tactical setup strongly favours the lone front runner Baandee, as she can set her own fractions without pace pressure, while the hold-up horses face the challenge of making up ground against a horse who won't tire from battling early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baandee Controls Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Baandee breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from the field
scenarios.body: She dictates comfortable fractions and has enough left to resist late challenges, making her turf debut successfully. The hold-up horses struggle to make up the deficit against an ungalloped leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fashion People Times Run
scenarios.trigger: If Fashion People gets the perfect trip tracking Baandee and produces her Newcastle winning form
scenarios.body: The class horse unleashes a sustained challenge in the final furlong, with Buick's timing proving decisive. Baandee's inexperience on turf shows when pressure arrives.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Baandee goes too fast early or struggles adapting from all-weather to turf
scenarios.body: The front runner ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for a closer. Fashion People or Night Shining benefit from the pace scenario falling apart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the market underestimates Venetian Sky's Newmarket promise or Night Shining's class
scenarios.body: The Haggas or Boughey runner produces significant improvement from their debut runs. The pace setup suits their patient tactics perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Baandee's turf adaptation is critical - any signs of struggling with the surface change could open the race up
Fashion People's long absence means watch for ring rustiness or lack of early pace positioning
Night Shining needs to break more alertly than at Newmarket where she was slowly away
The small field size means any non-runner would significantly alter the pace dynamics
Watch Venetian Sky for signs of the promise Haggas saw when running her at Newmarket as a newcomer

races.name: Gold & Silver Exchange Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Alpine Culture
runners_data.note: Front-runner faces no pace pressure and gets ideal tactical setup with Billy Loughnane's 5lb claim
runners_data.comment: Third at Newmarket (7f, good; 10-1) 16 days ago is probably the best form and 1m can help
runners_data.spotlight: Improved when third of eight in maiden at Newmarket (7f, good; 10-1) 16 days ago, always prominent and just ahead of Kimbara; that's probably the best form in this line-up and it looks as if 1m will help.

runners_data.name: Revelio
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 369-day break but has strong staying pedigree for the mile trip
runners_data.comment: Leicester 6th (1m2f) last April; left R Hannon for 25,000gns in July; gelding and wind op
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 7f 2yo/1m Listed winner who was runner-up in 1,000 Guineas; 18-1 from 12-1, faded into sixth of ten in maiden at Leicester (1m2f, good) last April; left Richard Hannon for 25,000gns in July, before gelding and wind operations early this year; work to do.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lion
runners_data.note: Unexposed newcomer with quality breeding but unknown pace style creates tactical uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Tenth foal; the dam's eight winners include seven with top RPRs of 101-116; one to note
runners_data.spotlight: By St Mark's Basilica; tenth foal; closely related to Group-placed 7.5f AW 2yo winner Golden Crown (RPR 104), half-brother to seven winners including Forest Of Dean (1m2f, including Group 3; 116), English Oak (7f/1m; 114) and Crown Of Oaks (1m/1m2f; 107); dam 6f/1m winner (98); withdrawn with self certificates in September and 12 days ago; newcomer to note.

runners_data.name: Fahidi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up in trip but showed fair form last summer before 238-day absence
runners_data.comment: Carries head high but still enters calculations after showing fair form on both 2yo starts
runners_data.spotlight: Some market support when showing fair form in a maiden at Sandown (7f, good) last July and novice at Haydock (1m, good) in September; carries head high but still enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Euston Hall
runners_data.note: Prominent type with decent form ratings who should appreciate the return to turf surface

runners_data.name: Adamlyi
runners_data.note: Lightly raced but disappointed as favourite last time and faces 216 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Gambled on at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last September but ended up fifth of eight
runners_data.spotlight: Kingman half-brother to Mujtaba (Group-placed 7.5f-1m2f; RPR 118); gambled-on co-favourite for maiden at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last September but ended up fifth of eight, running green; very early days and it will be interesting to see if his backers return.

runners_data.name: Kimbara
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed improvement at Newmarket 16 days ago but needs pace to develop
runners_data.comment: About 3l fourth of 8 at Newmarket (7f, good; 50-1) 16 days ago, just behind Alpine Culture
runners_data.spotlight: Only fourth of five at Newcastle (6f, AW) on debut in March but much better when about 3l fourth of eight in maiden at Newmarket (7f, good; 50-1) 16 days ago, just over 1l behind Alpine Culture; that puts him in the mix and he can probably improve again.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Rear runner with poor form figures who historically fades in the closing stages
runners_data.comment: Behind at Nottingham (8.5f, soft; 28-1) in October and Southwell (1m; 100-1) 15 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Beat only one rival at Nottingham (8.5f, soft; 28-1) in October and two at Southwell (1m, AW; 100-1) 15 days ago.

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Tail-ender with weak recent form who finished last in both starts on similar going
runners_data.comment: 40-1 and 125-1 when last at Newmarket (1m) in October and Nottingham (1m2f) recently
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 and 125-1 when always towards rear at Newmarket (1m, good) in October and Nottingham (1m2f, good) three weeks ago, finishing last.

races.paceDynamic: Alpine Culture will set the pace alone from the front with minimal early pressure in this thin field of nine. The leading three-year-old has shown consistent front-running ability and faces no other confirmed pace-setters, allowing him to dictate comfortable fractions. Behind him, prominent runners like Revelio, Fahidi and Euston Hall will track in second and third, while the hold-up horses Kimbara, Ziggy's Avenger and That Darn Cantor sit towards the rear waiting to strike. This uncontested pace scenario strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can secure good early positions without expending energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Culture gets soft fractions on the front end without early pressure
scenarios.body: He can kick clear in the straight with energy reserves intact while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from deep positions. The flat Yarmouth track and good going conditions suit his sustained pace-setting style perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Culture sets steady pace but gets collared by a closer in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The patient prominent runners like Fahidi or Euston Hall can track the leader cheaply before quickening past him late. Their superior class ratings suggest they have more acceleration once positioned handily.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and bunches the field for a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Kimbara can utilise his finishing kick from the rear as he showed promise when fourth at Newmarket last time. The condensed field would suit his come-from-behind style if he gets racing room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to handle the step up in trip or race fitness concerns show
scenarios.body: Revelio returns from a long break with strong breeding for the distance and could outrun his odds. His dam's Group 1 connections suggest untapped ability despite the lengthy absence.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Culture could get uncontested lead and prove impossible to peg back if fractions suit
Venetian Lion represents powerful Haggas yard and could show significant improvement on debut
Revelio's lengthy absence may hide fitness but breeding suggests he wants every yard of this trip
Hold-up horses like Kimbara need genuine pace to aim at but may find little to work with
Fahidi carries head high which could indicate temperament issues under pressure in finish

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap

runners_data.name: Grindleton
runners_data.note: Handicap debutant from top yard could improve significantly, but 203 days off track creates fitness doubts despite prominent running style suiting the pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Makes his handicap debut and some improvement should be forthcoming this season
runners_data.spotlight: Not far away at Pontefract or Bath (again 1m on good to soft) last autumn on his second and third starts; makes his handicap debut and some improvement should be forthcoming this season.

runners_data.name: Roserunner
runners_data.note: Strong all-weather form may not translate to turf debut, though prominent style fits tactical setup and Marco Botti stable in decent form recently.
runners_data.comment: AW win; turf debut with cheekpieces, needing to bounce back from a modest show in January
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Lingfield novice (1m, AW) in December on second start and narrowly beaten on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.5f, AW) in January; however, this turf debut with first-time cheekpieces requires him to bounce back from a lesser show in late January.

runners_data.name: Sports Day
runners_data.note: Improved effort here 19 days ago suggests fitness and track knowledge, hold-up style perfectly suited to expected pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Close third here (1m, good) on handicap/seasonal debut, shaping as if 1m2f may well help
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after 2yo campaign and improved when a close, always-prominent third of eight here (1m, good) on handicap/seasonal debut 19 days ago, shaping as if 1m2f may well help; major player.

runners_data.name: Heart Sign
runners_data.note: Turf debut questions remain unanswered despite hold-up style fitting the race shape, trainer struggling for winners recently at 0/12.
runners_data.comment: Has not made a serious impact in his two handicaps, though probably stayed 1m2f last time
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten far on second or third starts but he's not made a serious impact since in his two handicaps (probably stayed 1m2f last time); this is his first turf race since debut.

runners_data.name: Alice De Clare
runners_data.note: Impressive Beverley win shows current form and finishing kick, though quick turnaround from seven days ago might catch up late in race.
runners_data.comment: Big move to take lead at Beverley (1m2f) last Thursday but beaten a neck; due to go up 7lb
runners_data.spotlight: Looked an interesting handicap debutante at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm) last Thursday and so it proved, as she made a big move from rear to lead over 1f out but was beaten a neck; due to go up 7lb after this, so has a good chance if she's in the same form on this quick return to action.

runners_data.name: Time To Sparkle
runners_data.note: Course experience valuable but prominent style less favoured than hold-up rivals given expected moderate early gallop from King's Courtier.
runners_data.comment: Short-head win at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW); didn't shape as well as Sports Day here latest
runners_data.spotlight: Saddle slipped three starts ago but she made amends with a short-head win at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in March; not discredited in fifth of eight here (1m, good) 19 days ago but she raced too freely and didn't shape as well as third-placed Sports Day.

runners_data.name: King's Courtier
runners_data.note: Only front-runner creates tactical advantage but history of fading suggests stamina doubts, though 5lb claim helps his burden significantly.
runners_data.comment: Better in AW maiden (9.4f) three weeks ago; needs to build on that on this handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed little in three starts last year (6f-1m) but much better when fourth of eight when 66-1 in maiden at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) three weeks ago; needs to build on that on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: King's Courtier provides the sole confirmed early leader, setting up a controlled gallop without pressure from the gate. The prominent runners Grindleton, Roserunner and Time To Sparkle will track closely but none are aggressive pace-pressers. This creates a measured tempo that allows the hold-up horses Alice De Clare, Heart Sign and Sports Day to get into contention from off the pace. The sustainable gallop and lack of early pace pressure heavily favours the hold-up brigade who can time their runs perfectly in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If King's Courtier sets his usual honest gallop without being pressed hard early
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows Alice De Clare and Sports Day to position perfectly and unleash their finishing kicks. Both showed strong late pace recently and this tactical setup plays directly into their hands.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Roserunner or Grindleton can position ideally tracking the leader and kick clear
scenarios.body: The handicap debutant angle works for Grindleton or Roserunner's all-weather form translates effectively to turf. They avoid the tactical complexities and strike when the pace lifts approaching the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: King's Courtier Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays extremely sedate and King's Courtier finds significant improvement
scenarios.body: His recent fourth at Wolverhampton suggests better form and with claim reducing his burden, he could steal this. The lack of early pressure allows him to dictate throughout and hold on grimly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop becomes pedestrian and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over the final two furlongs favouring horses with instant acceleration. Time To Sparkle's recent course form gives her the edge in a bunched finish where track knowledge matters.

watchPoints.text: King's Courtier's early fractions will determine the entire race shape - if he goes too slow it becomes a sprint finish favouring different horses entirely
Alice De Clare's quick turnaround from Beverley success seven days ago could impact her finishing kick in the final furlong
Grindleton's market movement given 203-day absence and handicap debut - any strong support suggests the Kubler yard expects significant improvement
Sports Day's position turning for home after showing improved form here recently - needs to be handy to utilise his strong finishing kick
Roserunner's turf debut adaptation from all-weather success - early positioning will indicate how well he's handling the surface change

races.name: Download The At The Races App Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Golden Horse
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 222-day layoff with strong connections but faces another confirmed pace-setter in small field
runners_data.comment: After three races (one win) this handicap debutant could still do better but it is needed
runners_data.spotlight: 425,000gns yearling by Sea The Stars; fair form last July-September on all three starts, though apparently best when off the mark in a weak race at Hamilton (1m, good; made all) on second occasion; well beaten in a 1m2f Newmarket novice on final outing; after only three races, this handicap debutant could still be capable of better but it is needed.

runners_data.name: Clouds Hill
runners_data.note: Lead horse with solid recent form who should engage Golden Horse early, creating the key pace dynamic

runners_data.name: A Major Payne
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well over course and distance recently and benefits from the expected honest early gallop
runners_data.comment: 0-15 but in some tight finishes at 1m and another over C&D recently on second go at 1m2f
runners_data.spotlight: 0-15 but involved in some tight finishes at 1m and also over C&D recently on his second go at 1m2f (one place ahead of Beach Point); off the same mark, he should be seriously involved if the returning cheekpieces (worn on penultimate start last term, ran creditably) don't have a negative effect.

runners_data.name: Lordsbridge Blu
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally positioned to track the pace battle and strike when the leaders weaken
runners_data.comment: 1-15 in handicaps but often thereabouts, including on turf and AW just three days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 1-15 in handicaps, with the win on Lingfield AW (AW) last November but he's often been thereabouts, including on turf; bang there on Wolverhampton AW on both outings this term, the latest just three days ago; player.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with cheekpieces fitted who needs the front-runners to maintain their effort to set up his late kick
runners_data.comment: C&D recently saw him finish on the heels of A Major Payne; should be competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Sandown (1m2f) last summer in first two starts after cheekpieces were refitted; respectable in two of four starts since, including over C&D recently when finishing on the heels of A Major Payne; should be competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Golden Horse and Clouds Hill are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the start. With only five runners, the two pace-setters will likely maintain a decent clip through the middle stages, preventing this from becoming a crawl. A Major Payne and Beach Point as hold-up horses will need the leaders to maintain their effort, while Lordsbridge Blu sits in the prominent position to track the pace. This race shape favors horses that can sit close to the pace and kick, as the two leaders may compromise each other's finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dual Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Horse and Clouds Hill engage in a prolonged speed duel from the start
scenarios.body: The two leaders will weaken significantly in the final furlong, allowing the prominent tracker to capitalize on their honest work. Lordsbridge Blu gets the ideal setup to strike late from his tracking position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Horse or Clouds Hill establishes a clear early advantage without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader maintains energy for a strong finish while the other front-runner fades from chasing. The winner gets soft fractions early and has enough left to repel late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners maintain a genuinely strong gallop throughout without collapsing
scenarios.body: The honest pace sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses to unleash their finishing kicks. A Major Payne and Beach Point benefit from the strong early tempo created by the dual pace angle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders breaks clear early and the other fails to engage in a speed duel
scenarios.body: The remaining front-runner gets uncontested fractions and builds an insurmountable lead on the small field. With limited pressure throughout, they maintain enough energy to hold off all challengers.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Golden Horse shows any ring-rust from his 222-day absence as this could leave Clouds Hill uncontested on the lead
Monitor the early fractions between Golden Horse and Clouds Hill - if one submits quickly the race shape changes dramatically
Observe Lordsbridge Blu's early positioning as he holds the key tactical advantage if the pace scenario unfolds
Check if A Major Payne can secure a clear passage in the straight with only five runners limiting room for maneuver
Watch Beach Point's response to pressure as his hold-up style needs the pace battle to materialize properly

races.name: Sky Sports Virgin 512 Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the expected strong pace but 181 days off the track is a significant concern for race fitness
runners_data.comment: Better is needed over this new trip on return but her stable is in fine form
runners_data.spotlight: 6f maiden and novice winner on good to firm last June/July; ran further good races when fourth of 12 in a Doncaster nursery (6.5f, good to soft) and eighth in a Newmarket Listed race (6f, good); better is needed over this new trip on return but her stable is in fine form, including with two recent 3yo reappearance winners.

runners_data.name: Moonshine
runners_data.note: James Doyle's prominent tactics ideal for this pace scenario with solid recent form keeping her sharp
runners_data.comment: Return to 7f looks in order and she seems to have a competitive mark for handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Second at 2-5 and evens after catching the eye on Newbury debut (finished third) but she made no mistake in a four-runner novice at Kempton (6f, AW) six weeks ago and the odds-on runner-up won next time; return to 7f looks in order and, although this handicap debut is more of a test, she seems to have a competitive mark.

runners_data.name: You'll Think Of Me
runners_data.note: Natural leader but 150-day break questions her ability to sustain a speed duel against fresher opponents
runners_data.comment: Progressive Irish form before off the mark when 1-3 at Kempton (6f, AW) in December
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to win in four runs for Donnacha O'Brien in Ireland but she showed progressive form for him and made a winning debut for new yard in five-runner novice at Kempton (6f, AW) in December; the latter was at 1-3, admittedly, but she stays 7f and goes on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with crucial 15-day fitness edge but faces three other pace rivals in what could become a suicidal battle
runners_data.comment: Steady progress on AW; strength at finish last time makes this 7f an appealing option
runners_data.spotlight: Steadily going the right way, on last two starts winning in a novice at Wolverhampton in November and handicap debut at Southwell 15 days ago; both of those were 6f on AW under good claimer Jack Callan; up 6lb but strength at the finish last time makes 7f today an appealing option.

runners_data.name: Here I Bow
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to the expected pace collapse but 206 days absent raises serious fitness doubts
runners_data.comment: 7f maiden winner last June from seven starts in France; peak efforts on softer than good
runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; dam lightly raced, placed in Germany at 1m1f, out of unraced half-sister to German 1m Group 2 and US 1m2f Grade 2 winner Sumitas; 7f maiden win last June from seven starts in France for Florian Guyander; peak efforts on softer than good; marked improvement is seemingly needed on British debut; rookie trainer's reappearance winner this month was heavily backed.

runners_data.name: Wetsand
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent poor form is offset by Tom Marquand's tactical awareness in pace-heavy scenarios
runners_data.comment: Out of form in 10.5f Listed race at Saint-Cloud (heavy) and 7f handicap at Southwell (AW)
runners_data.spotlight: In good form in her early starts on turf last year but soundly beaten facing much stiffer tasks on next two outings; remained out of form this season in 10.5f Listed race at Saint-Cloud (heavy) and 7f handicap at Southwell (AW) and that's a major worry.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Angel
runners_data.note: Front-running style hampered by 7lb claiming rider and 208-day layoff against sharper rivals
runners_data.comment: Outclassed in valuable sales race in October but progressive going into that; 7lb claimer
runners_data.spotlight: Outclassed in a valuable sales race in October but progressive going into that, culminating in a front-running win on handicap debut at Newmarket (7f, good to firm); 5lb higher for this return and 7lb claimer is recruited.

runners_data.name: Angels' Share
runners_data.note: Natural leader whose 218-day absence makes her vulnerable in what promises to be a demanding speed battle
runners_data.comment: 7f on Lingfield AW for quick double last summer; player if back to best for in-form yard
runners_data.spotlight: 7f on Lingfield AW for her quick double late last summer in a maiden and nursery, both from the front; did those in some style but found a hot fillies' race at Goodwood (7f, good to soft) in September far too demanding; player if back to her best for a yard that seems to be in good form.

races.paceDynamic: Zighy, You'll Think Of Me, Harlequin Angel and Angels' Share will all look to lead or be prominent early, creating a fierce battle for the front over 7f at Yarmouth. This quartet of front-runners will force a genuine end-to-end gallop with no let-up from flag to finish. The relentless pace will stretch the field out and test stamina reserves in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can capitalise on the inevitable pace collapse, while pure front-runners face the difficult task of surviving their own speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners engage in a speed duel through halfway
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop will set up perfectly for hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong. Here I Bow's patient style under Coakley becomes a major tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If one horse can sit just off the early pace without getting involved in the speed battle
scenarios.body: A prominent racer can time their move perfectly as the leaders tire, striking at the ideal moment with fresher reserves. Brisk Symphony or Moonshine can exploit this tactical position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate terms and moderate the early fractions
scenarios.body: Zighy's recent winning form could see him control the pace and kick clear when others expect him to stop. His fitness advantage from a 15-day break may prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sustained Speed Battle
scenarios.trigger: If all four front-runners refuse to give ground and maintain maximum pressure throughout
scenarios.body: The pace becomes so strong that even the hold-up horses struggle to make up the ground, leading to a messy finish where stamina matters most. Form may go out the window in a war of attrition.

watchPoints.text: Zighy and You'll Think Of Me could engage in a match race from the gates given both are confirmed front-runners with similar tactical approaches
Here I Bow's jumping from the rear may struggle if the pace is so strong that even hold-up horses can't make up the ground
Moonshine and Brisk Symphony positioning in the first furlong will reveal if they can avoid the early speed battle
The four front-runners could create such genuine pace that 7f becomes a stamina test favouring the more experienced campaigners
Angels' Share under Fallon may try to steal a march if the other leaders hesitate at the start

races.name: Eastern Power Systems 'Confined' Handicap (For horses Which Have Won No More Than One Race)

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Hold-up type relying on Tom Marquand's tactical skills but may struggle to make up ground on good to firm going after 21 days off
runners_data.comment: Chased home 1-2 shot in maiden latest; return to 1m may help and cheekpieces are enlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing at 5-4 for handicap debut (1m, good) to end last season and reappearance in Wolverhampton maiden (9.4f, AW) wasn't his best form either, albeit providing the most resistance to a 1-2 favourite and 5l clear of the rest; return to 1m might help and cheekpieces are enlisted.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing improved handicap form for Ed Walker but needs the pace to collapse to be effective from the rear
runners_data.comment: Improved form when a close third of 12 on seasonal/handicap debut at Nottingham (1m, good)
runners_data.spotlight: Useful pedigree and he showed improved form when a close third of 12 on seasonal/handicap debut at Nottingham (1m, good) three weeks ago, favourite and mounting a strong challenge in the final 1f; up 3lb but strong chance.

runners_data.name: Armstrong
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good current form with just 13 days since last run, well-positioned to track Okiru's uncontested lead

runners_data.name: Okiru
runners_data.note: Sole front runner switching to turf debut with Harry Vigors' 7lb claim, perfectly positioned to exploit the lack of early pace pressure
runners_data.comment: 0-7, all 7f on AW; sent handicapping on his last three starts; ran well in the first two
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7, all over 7f on AW; sent handicapping on his last three starts; ran well in the first two of those before a lesser show in second-time cheekpieces on latest; 7lb claimer is enlisted for this turf debut with in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Norfolk Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 224-day layoff which creates significant fitness concerns despite useful form when fresh
runners_data.comment: Novice 2nd at Lingfield (7f, good to soft) in July stands out from his other four efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Second from off the pace in a novice at Lingfield (7f, good to soft) last July on second start but that stands out a mile from his other four performances; stamina on the dam's side; gelded prior to this reappearance for an in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with tendency to fade in finish, making his task even harder from the rear in this pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Promise from off the pace when third of nine on handicap debut here (7f, good) in October
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after third start last season and took third of nine on handicap debut here (7f, good) in October on his only appearance since; showed promise too, from off the pace, and isn't entirely ruled out despite the need for further progress.

races.paceDynamic: Okiru is the sole confirmed front runner and will face no early pressure, allowing him to dictate a comfortable tempo through the early stages. Armstrong may track prominently but lacks the pure pace to challenge Okiru's lead, while the majority of the field (Zooter, Del Corso, Guest House) are hold-up types who need to be delivered late. Norfolk Blue sits between prominent and hold-up but has been absent for 224 days. This uncontested pace scenario strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the tempo without having to make ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Okiru Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Okiru breaks cleanly and faces no early pressure from Armstrong
scenarios.body: He dictates ideal fractions and kicks clear turning for home, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up significant ground on good to firm going. The lack of pace pressure allows the leader to save energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too steady and Okiru stops in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their preferred scenario with a sprint finish, allowing Zooter or Del Corso to unleash their finishing kicks. Tom Marquand's tactical awareness could prove decisive on Zooter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Armstrong Applies Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Armstrong travels strongly and puts Okiru under pressure from the halfway point
scenarios.body: The increased tempo sets up perfectly for Armstrong's prominent style while compromising Okiru's stamina reserves. David Egan positions Armstrong to strike approaching the final furlong when Okiru begins to weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Norfolk Blue Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Norfolk Blue overcomes his 224-day absence and runs to his best Lingfield form
scenarios.body: His prominent style benefits from tracking the uncontested pace, and Cieren Fallon times his challenge perfectly. The good to firm ground suits his profile better than his recent all-weather efforts.

watchPoints.text: Norfolk Blue's fitness after 224 days absence - any market support would be significant given the layoff concerns
Okiru's jump from all-weather to turf debut - his front-running style needs to translate effectively to the surface
Armstrong's early positioning behind Okiru - David Egan's tactics will determine if he applies pressure or sits quietly
Guest House's finishing effort given his tendency to fade - needs to show more sustained effort than typical pattern
The pace through the opening two furlongs - if too steady it could bring the hold-up horses into contention
